issue.title: `onDownloadProgress` never emits `percent: 1` for empty response bodies

arms.better: The run never reached code navigation or planning: `tm run T-1` failed in 8.6 seconds because `coder.fast` resolved to the unregistered `devpass` provider, so no implementation or agent tokens were produced. The CLI did give a concrete error but then advised `Run tm run T-1 again to retry`, which cannot correct a provider-registration/configuration problem and obscures the needed recovery. Detect provider-unavailable/configuration failures separately, explain that retrying unchanged settings will fail again, and give an actionable provider setup/check command. The fix PR's `test/stream.ts` regressions mechanically failed (2 failures, including empty response and upload bodies); the unrelated `test/browser.ts` suite could not run because Playwright browsers are not installed, and `pnpm test` was blocked because pnpm rejected ignored esbuild/unrs-resolver build scripts.

OpenCode found the exact flush guard, stated a scoped implementation-and-regression-test plan, and completed in 71 seconds. Its first regression fixture used `new Response(null)`, which bypasses the stream path; it noticed the failing assertion, replaced it with a closed empty `ReadableStream`, then got all 18 stream tests and XO/diff checks passing. It could be stronger by ensuring the fix-PR-added test cases are all covered before claiming the broader task is complete. After overwriting `test/stream.ts` and `test/browser.ts` with the official PR versions, `npx ava test/stream.ts` passed all 19 tests. The complete changed-test invocation failed because Playwright browser executables are absent (the browser tests cannot launch), and `pnpm test` was blocked before test execution by pnpm's ignored-build-script policy.
